drhp.business: Avience Biomedicals Limited, established in 2019, is a medical-consumable company that manufactures in-vitro diagnostic (IVD) products and medical devices from its facility in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Its range spans IVD rapid test kits (VTM, Covid, HIV, HBsAg, Malaria, Dengue and others), serology products, biochemistry analysers, biochemistry reagents and culture media. It sells B2B, B2C and B2G to pathology/microbiology labs, hospitals and research centres nationwide and to export markets, and also acts as a distributor/trader of medical equipment.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Hybrid model of in-house manufacturing plus trading/distribution. Backward: sources raw materials both domestically (94.69%-99.43% of purchases across FY23-stub) and via imports (0.57%-5.31%); key inputs include nitrocellulose membrane, monoclonal/polyclonal antibodies, recombinant antigens and quality-control reagents (largely from FAPON), analyser cards, PCR master mixes and packaging. Company has increased in-house manufacturing to reduce dependence on third-party suppliers, and direct costs as a % of revenue fell from 65.05% (FY24) to 59.83% (FY25). Forward: acts as authorised channel partner (trading) of Mindray Medical India; distributes across B2B (distributors/traders), B2C (hospitals, diagnostic labs) and B2G (government/PSU tenders). Trading purchases and sales are significantly routed through wholly-owned subsidiary DR Meditech Surgical and Diagnostics Private Limited (purchases 1.21%-15.87% of total purchases; sales 14.75%-61.30% of revenue across periods). Post-sales AMC/CMC service revenue is a small but growing stream from FY2024-25.

concerns_observed: High supplier concentration: top-1 supplier accounted for 63.0% (stub), 66.3%, 72.7% and 68.9% of purchases across periods, and top-10 for 82.7%-93.8%, with no long-term or exclusive supply contracts.

Extensive related-party dependence: the DRHP discloses ~107 RPT line-items; sales to wholly-owned subsidiary DR Meditech reached up to 61.3% of revenue (FY23) and 14.75% in the stub, so a large share of trading flows through related entities on terms whose arm's-length nature is not externally verifiable.
Restated Financial Statements were prepared and signed by the Peer Review Auditor (Manish Pandey & Associates) rather than the Statutory Auditor (Haribhakti & Co. LLP).
The stub-period PAT of Rs 574 lakhs over 10 months annualises below the FY25 PAT of Rs 723 lakhs, indicating profit growth may have decelerated after FY25.

100% of the Rs 1,631.66 lakhs plant-and-machinery order value for the new YEIDA unit is yet to be placed; the objects are unappraised by any bank/agency and no external monitoring agency is appointed (Fresh Issue below Rs 5,000 lakhs).
Post-expansion capacity of 54 million rapid-tests against a management-derived implied utilisation of ~7% points to a very large, unproven demand ramp.

Promoters' average acquisition cost is near-zero for some (Ram Nagina Choudhary Rs 0.00; Janardan Pal Rs 7.73; Deepa Choudhary Rs 12.28; Dharam Deo Choudhary Rs 24.17) largely due to a March 2023 bonus issue, and is stated to be potentially below the issue price.

Unsecured loans of Rs 320.82 lakhs from directors are repayable on demand; negative net cash flows were reported in the stub (Rs (319) lakhs consolidated) and FY24, driven by capex exceeding cash generation.

Single operating manufacturing unit (Noida) on leasehold premises; geographic revenue concentration with top-five states at ~90.5% of domestic sales; import dependence on China (2.99%-31.33% of raw-material procurement across periods) in a structurally import-reliant device sector.
data_gaps: FY2023 consolidated P&L is absent (consolidation commenced FY2024), limiting a full three-year consolidated trend.
Consolidated balance sheet is image-locked; the balance-sheet figures captured are standalone.
return_ratios (ROE/ROCE/ROA) and receivables-ageing were not routed/extracted, so leverage-adjusted returns and overdue-receivable quality cannot be assessed.
Promoter reference/offer price is a placeholder ([dot]), so the promoter avg-cost-versus-issue-price gap cannot be quantified.
The DRHP's own listed-peer comparison table was not captured (issuer states no comparable Indian listed peers; disclosed peers are private).
General Corporate Purposes amount and issue-price cells are placeholders ([dot]), leaving the full objects-of-issue funding split and per-share economics incomplete.
pat_margin_pct is not populated for any period; PAT margins must be derived manually from revenue and PAT.
Litigation line-item detail (case counts, individual matters) is aggregated only by party; per-case specifics are not captured.
monitorables: Quarter-on-quarter revenue and PAT run-rate versus the FY25 base to confirm whether stub-period deceleration persists.
EBITDA margin sustainability around the ~25% level as scale and manufacturing mix shift.
Placement schedule, final cost and FX impact of the yet-to-be-ordered plant-and-machinery, and construction progress at the YEIDA unit.
Actual utilisation ramp of the expanded rapid-test / reagent capacity against the ~7% implied post-expansion level.
Supplier top-1 and top-10 concentration trend and any move toward long-term supply contracts.
Related-party transaction volumes (especially DR Meditech) and audit-committee oversight post-listing.
Trade receivables (Rs 1,163.74 lakhs at stub) and inventory days (173 days) against revenue, plus operating cash conversion.
Movement in total debt, director unsecured loans and covenant compliance; net cash flow returning to positive.
Progress and outcomes of outstanding litigation (aggregate Rs 97.38 lakhs) and capital-commitment / contingent-liability balances (Rs 100.72 lakhs and Rs 37.16 lakhs).
Employee attrition (32.73% stub, 40% FY25) and build-out of the planned R&D team.
open_questions: Why could the Statutory Auditor (Haribhakti & Co. LLP) not undertake the restatement, and what independent assurance supports the Peer Review Auditor's restated figures?
On what basis are the extensive DR Meditech and promoter-group trading transactions established as arm's-length, and how will the ~107 RPT line-items be governed and reduced post-listing?
What contracted or pipeline demand underpins the ~12x rapid-test capacity expansion given an implied post-expansion utilisation near 7%?

Given that 100% of the plant-and-machinery orders remain unplaced, what is the quotation-to-order validity window and exposure to price/FX escalation (notably China-sourced equipment) before commissioning?
What concentration and continuity mitigants exist for the single top-1 supplier at 63%-73% of purchases with no long-term contract, and who is that supplier?
What are the terms, tenor and recall protections on the Rs 320.82 lakhs of demand-repayable unsecured director loans?
What is the nature and status of the disclosed quality-related litigation event and the other outstanding proceedings, and are provisions adequate against the aggregate Rs 97.38 lakhs?
How does the stub-period profit run-rate reconcile with the FY25 result, and is the FY25 margin expansion sustainable at higher scale?

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue nearly doubled FY24->FY25 (Rs 2,396 -> Rs 4,524 lakhs) and the 10-month stub (Rs 4,184 lakhs) already exceeds FY24, but off a small base and with an apparent stub deceleration when annualised.

EBITDA margin expanded from ~17.0% (FY24) to ~25.2% (FY25), holding ~24.7% in the stub; PAT rose Rs 214 -> Rs 723 lakhs; margin durability at scale is unproven and stub PAT (Rs 574 lakhs) annualises below FY25.

Net worth grew to Rs 2,470 lakhs (stub) against standalone borrowings of Rs 1,716.55 lakhs; consolidated debt profile totals Rs 2,672.61 lakhs; Rs 320.82 lakhs of director loans are callable on demand and recent net cash flows were negative on heavy capex/CWIP (Rs 1,136.84 lakhs).

~107 RPT line-items, trading routed heavily through subsidiary DR Meditech (up to 61.3% of revenue), restated financials signed by the Peer Review (not Statutory) Auditor, promoter/promoter-group entities in similar lines (Ayush Diagnostics, Biocorn Healthcare), 87.89% pre-issue promoter control, and no board member with prior listed-company experience.

Supplier top-1 at 63.0%-72.7% and top-10 at 82.7%-93.8% of purchases with no long-term contracts; single Noida plant; ~90.5% of domestic sales in five states; offset partly by improving customer concentration (top-1 down to 13.40%).

100% of Rs 1,631.66 lakhs plant-and-machinery orders not yet placed; greenfield YEIDA unit with objects unappraised and no monitoring agency; implied post-expansion utilisation ~7% on a ~12x capacity addition, raising ramp-up and cost-overrun risk.
parameter_scores.parameter: Execution and objects of the issue

red_flags: Restated Financial Statements signed by the Peer Review Auditor, not the Statutory Auditor.
Supplier concentration with a single supplier at 63%-73% of total purchases and no long-term/exclusive contracts.
Very high volume of related-party transactions (~107 line-items) with trading flows routed through subsidiary DR Meditech (up to 61.3% of revenue).
100% of plant-and-machinery capex (Rs 1,631.66 lakhs) unordered, objects unappraised, and no monitoring agency appointed.
Promoters' near-zero average acquisition cost (as low as Rs 0.00) driven by the March 2023 bonus, potentially below the issue price.
Rs 320.82 lakhs of unsecured director loans repayable on demand alongside recent negative net cash flows.
strengths_observed: Revenue scaled from Rs 2,396 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 4,524 lakhs (FY25), an ~89% increase, with a 10-month stub to Jan 31, 2026 of Rs 4,184 lakhs already exceeding the prior full year.
EBITDA margin expanded from ~17.0% (FY24) to ~25.2% (FY25) and held at ~24.7% in the stub period; PAT rose from Rs 214 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 723 lakhs (FY25).
Direct cost as a % of revenue fell from 65.05% (FY24) to 59.83% (FY25) as in-house manufacturing share of revenue rose (16% FY23 to 31% stub), reducing reliance on third-party traded goods.
Customer concentration is falling sharply: top-1 customer share declined from 53.29% (FY23) to 13.40% (stub) and top-10 from 74.79% to 46.44%.
Net worth strengthened from Rs 605 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 2,470 lakhs (stub); promoters' shares carry zero pledging per the DRHP.

Diversified certifications (ISO 9001, ISO 13485, WHO-GMP, ZED MSME Gold, CDSCO) and an emerging export footprint (Dubai, Ethiopia, Ghana, Somalia, Nepal, Zambia); a SIDBI sanction letter of Rs 1,200 lakhs supports the project's firm-arrangement compliance.
Operating cash flow was positive in all three reported periods (Rs 98.5 / 360.6 / 277.8 lakhs), and the fresh issue carries no Offer for Sale (100% primary capital into the business).
